subject: Post-demo: encryption, KMS options & vendor questionnaire (CardioTech)
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Anya Petrova <anya@cardiotech.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-08-01T14:03:00-07:00
Subject: Post-demo: encryption, KMS options & vendor questionnaire (CardioTech)

Hi Anya / Matt —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and next steps so we have alignment: we covered how Redwood protects customer data in transit and at rest, the KMS/HSM options for private vs hosted deployments, and the path for customer-managed keys (BYOK).

Key points from the call:
- SOC 2: Redwood completed SOC 2 Type I in 2026; Type II run is in progress with expected availability in Q3 2027 (summary attached). Full report access is part of our enterprise package and we can start an NDA if you need the full artifact.
- GDPR / HIPAA: We offer Data Processing Agreements and HIPAA BAAs for covered customers. CardioTech’s use case (PHI) will require the BAA and private deployment discussion.
- Encryption at-rest: All customer data is encrypted using AES-256-GCM at rest with envelope encryption. Root/master keys are handled via KMS integrations or Redwood-managed keys depending on deployment.
- In-transit: TLS 1.2+ with support for TLS 1.3. For Private deployments we can enable mTLS for service-to-service connections.
- KMS/HSM options: three broad patterns we discussed:
  1) Redwood-managed keys: simplest operational model (we manage root keys; envelope encryption at the application layer).
  2) Customer-managed cloud KMS (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault): you bring a CMK and we integrate via our key policy; supports key rotation and Cloud KMS access controls.
  3) BYO-HSM / EKM: for private deployments we support HSM-backed master keys (FIPS 140-2 level 3/4 options via partner HSMs). We support PKCS#11 integrations or wrapped-import (RSA-OAEP) for import where applicable.

Operational notes / asks:
- Please start the vendor security questionnaire (attached) when convenient — we filled out the sections we can and marked items needing product/infra detail.
- For BYOK flow: we provide a wrapped-key import guide; if you need a partner HSM integration (e.g., Luna/Thales), let us know your vendor and we’ll coordinate a technical workshop.
- Audit logs & key rotation: key usage audit events are retained in our Console and can be exported to your SIEM (Syslog/Cloud Pub/Sub options). We support rotation schedules and can export key rotation records for audits.

Next steps:
1) Anya/Matt: complete the questionnaire and mark any “requires evidence” items.
2) Redwood: share the SOC 2 summary + the KMS options one-pager (attached) and sample key-import instructions.
3) Schedule a 60-minute technical deep dive with your infra/security engineers to walk the BYOK/HSM flow. Suggested windows: next week (Tue/Wed afternoon PST).

Attachments: redwood_SOC2_summary_2027-06.pdf, redwood_kms_options_onepager.pdf, sample_key_import_instructions.txt

Thanks — happy to jump on video to demo any of the flows.

—Sean
Sean Gallagher
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

3) Audit logs: are KMS key-usage logs exportable to our Splunk instance? If so, what is the retention and format?

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>

Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Matt Reynolds <matt.reynolds@cardiotech.com>
Date: 2027-08-01T18:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: encryption, KMS options & vendor questionnaire (CardioTech)

Hi Anya — quick answers inline and some follow-up detail.

1) SOC 2 Type II timing: our audit run is scheduled to complete the evaluation week of 2027-09-20; we expect to be able to share the Type II report under NDA by the first week of October (approx. 2027-10-04). The attached SOC2 summary includes the scope and auditor firm. If you need earlier artifacts we can provide control narratives and test evidence snapshots under NDA now.

2) EKM/HSM model: for our hosted offering the typical supported pattern is:
   - Customer-managed cloud KMS (AWS/GCP/Azure): Redwood calls the KMS for envelope key unwrap operations. The key material never resides unwrapped in our services. This meets the requirement that master keys are controlled by your KMS; however the KMS service itself is in the cloud provider control plane.
   - For an on-prem/private deployment we support HSM-backed keys where the HSM is customer-controlled and connected to the Redwood Private runtime via a secure network path. In that model the HSM can serve unwrap operations (EKM) and the key material never leaves the HSM.
   - Wrapped-import: we also support wrapped-key import for situations where the HSM vendor provides an export function to create a wrapped blob. The import flow requires the wrapped blob to be uploaded to the Redwood key-import service (instructions attached).

If your policy requires the key to never be exportable under any condition, the on-prem HSM / EKM model is the recommended path. We’ll discuss details in the technical session and can bring an architect to map a deployment diagram.

3) Audit logs / Splunk: yes — key usage and KMS audit events can be forwarded to your Splunk via our event-forwarder. We export JSON lines with timestamps, key-id, operation (Encrypt/Decrypt/Sign), caller identity, and request-id. Retention depends on your plan (default 90 days in Console; longer retention available via enterprise add-on). We can also stream to S3/GCS or your SIEM (syslog/HTTPS).

Attached: redwood_kms_options_onepager.pdf, sample_key_import_instructions.txt, redwood_SOC2_summary_2027-06.pdf

Schedule: Wed 2027-08-04 10:00am PST works for us — I’ll accept the invite. For the deep dive we’ll bring our infra architect (Laura) and our security lead (Marissa). Please share your security engineer’s contact so we can share the pre-read.

Regards,
—Sean
